utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One matter to be dealt with outstanding from yesterday was the request by Mr. Fila and Mr. Petrovic to exclude part of the evidence of Dr. Rugova. The Chamber has considered this further and is of the view that this comes too late, it should have been dealt with at the time, but that in any event on the face of it it is an unsound application and therefore we refuse it. Can we now have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A number of problems arose in yesterday's evidence, and I have been giving some thought to how to deal with the situation to try to avoid a repetition of some of the problems we had yesterday. So I'm making a point at the outset of the evidence today of saying what I've said I think quite a number of times already. It's important that you focus on the particular point raised. We all recognise that you feel very strongly about certain things and you feel the need to ensure that we are absolutely fully informed. But please believe me that we have a considerable amount of material which we've already read from -- produced by you, and it is vital to concentrate on the particular points that counsel are raising. And if we feel we're not getting enough, we will ask questions ourselves. So I ask you to be patient with us and try to concentrate on the question. Similarly, I direct these words to counsel. Please try to focus the questions specifically and try, so far as possible, to avoid narrating paragraphs of material, after which it's sometimes very difficult to follow the question. In most cases yesterday, I think it would have been possible to ask a question without reference to the various paragraphs which were referred to. I appreciate that that happens in a limited number of questions, but when it does happen it tends to cloud, rather than clear, the issue that's before the Trial Chamber. And since I expect much of the proceedings this morning to be conducted in B/C/S, then please bear in mind the need to pause - and this applies to both counsel and witness - pause between question and answer so that you give the interpreters, who do a very difficult job here extremely well, but have -- naturally have limitations because of the difficulty of the job. Give them time to catch up. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have read the transcript and my notes carefully, and regardless of what you have just said, I have finished my cross-examination. I would like to thank you and I would like to thank Mr. Dorovic. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is not a criticism. I hope you will take it in the right spirit, but life is full of surprises. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dorovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I am Djuro Cepic, one of the Defence team members, and I am going to have some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up Exhibit 1309, P1309, in B/C/S page 7, in the English version page 30, Article 64. Can I please call that up on the screen. Can we focus on Article 64, please. Page 7 in B/C/S, page 30 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, on your chief on Monday conducted by Ms. Moeller you stated that the platoon commander is responsible and if he finds the perpetrator he has to arrest him. This was on page 11440 of the transcript here in Article 64, the first paragraph, it says: "Every officer holding the post of company commander or another equal or higher post and an authorised official of the internal affairs organ or the security organ of the Yugoslav Army forces and military police might arrest a serviceman caught in the act of committing a crime being prosecuted ex officio if there is the risk of his escaping or if that person poses a risk to life or important property." Can you see that, Mr. Dorovic? Paragraph 1 of Article 64, that is?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My question to you is this, please listen carefully: Am I right in saying that a company commander can arrest a person who has committed a crime if the conditions of this sort are in place, but that customarily it is the military security services that perform arrests because they're educated and trained and equipped to perform arrests?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is exactly what I emphasised.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask the registrar to put Exhibit Number P2818 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, before us on the screens there is information of the work of the military judiciary. You have already commented upon this information. You will agree with me, won't you, that this is not information from the Pristina Corps originally but that this information which is an -- a piece of information from the staff of the Supreme Command of the sector for operational work and training, the command of the Pristina Corps only forwarded it to somebody else. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't know what is in the enclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask the registrar to go to the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You can see information from the 1st Army and from the 2nd Army; in other words, this is not something that originates from the Pristina Corps, this is something that the Pristina Corps forwarded to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the stamp in the upper right-hand side corner I see "Belgrade," so that may well be the case. Can we see who signed it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the contents? It says in the 1st Army.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the information is from. I can't see it, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the last page on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, just now, you've just said that this is something the Pristina Corps forwarded to the General Staff. Did you mean to say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Opposite. Probably opposite, probably it is a problem in translation, because this document issued by general --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I understood that the first time and I thought this was the other way around, so I was just trying to correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be of assistance, this document we are looking at now contains the same thing as document P1918, which is already in the system, has been used through witness Vasiljevic. Only the cover page of this document differs from the cover page of the other one. In the document 1918 you can see who the author of the document is, where it originated from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, you have it now on your screen, don't you, the signatory --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no signatory. It says here that it was compiled, and as somebody who knows the system I am questioning the credibility of this document, not its contents but the formal aspect thereof --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, just a moment. Let's not go into such tiny details. Are you the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is what I'd like to hear. Can you read the first page.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I am asking you questions --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I am answering questions. I want to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, I am asking you very clear questions and I'm kindly asking you to answer my questions clearly and up to the point and I am grateful to you in advance to you for that. On the first page it says: "This command received information from the staff of the Supreme Command from the sector for operations and education," under number so-and-so. I am asking you a very simple question. This information which is enclosed to this document, is this something that was issued by the staff of the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please read it and you will see that it is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Dorovic, Pusto Selo, Senovac near Orahovac has been mentioned a location. You have also mentioned this as one of the case files missing.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never mentioned this, never mentioned the names of these places. Let's be precise, Mr. Cepic. I was talking --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Senovac near Orahovac --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about a mass grave in the vicinity of Orahovac containing 47 bodies. This is a case file that I had in my hands and the places that you mentioned -- the places that you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I will be very precise. The only mass grave that is mentioned near Orahovac is this one in Senovac. So we can call it a mass grave near Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about what is being mentioned, I'm also aware of some others around Orahovac --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this one --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters will not be able to interpret if the speakers overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, there's too much overlapping here. Now, I know you're not the principal offender at the moment, and I recognise that, but the witness has to be controlled by you and we've had more than a day of trying to learn how to do this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that counsel is too fast with his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I'm just being told that you speak too quickly and it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: He asks questions too quickly. It cannot be interpreted in its entirety. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have mentioned in these documents that you inspected with regard to that mass grave near Orahovac that a large number of documents were located, documents that were issued by the military police, and my question is this: Do you maybe know that the security organ of the command of the Pristina Corps immediately, when they learned about a number of fresh graves near Orahovac, sent its organs to check the information that had been received in the media through some individuals or from some units and to check the situation on the ground and see what had actually happened? Are you aware of that? As you were expecting those documents, did you learn of that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found a number of official notes by the security organs, if I remember it well, and one was signed by Nesic and I know that in particular note very well, because I know the person --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in other words, I'm aware of all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That answer's not very clear to me. Are you saying you were aware of a number of other mass graves which had been investigated by the military security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. In my answer I just said this -- the question was whether I knew that among the documents there were also official notes by the security organs. I said yes, and I specified that I was particularly interested and I analysed a note that was compiled by Nesic, the security organ, and there was some other official notes among those as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, Mr. Dorovic. The question was: Do you know that the security organ of the command of the Pristina Corps sent units to check the situation on the ground and see that this actually happened? Now, do you know that they looked for these reported mass graves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I am aware of only one grave, and this is the only one I'm talking about. This is the first time I hear that there might have been investigation into some others, that there were others investigated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you allow me, I asked a specific question about exactly that grave and he confirmed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, I see, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- and he confirmed in his answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see. Sorry. Well, the question was that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He confirmed that he found -- I'm sorry if I interrupt you. He confirmed in his statement in paragraph 35, he confirmed that he found the files with the records of security staff of -- and he mentioned the name of Nesic also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But if you look at your question again you say: "Do you maybe know that the security organ in the command of the Pristina Corps immediately, when they learned of a number of fresh graves near Orahovac," now I got --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, it was a single, not a plural --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The way it's come out in the translation I got suggests there were a number of sites but you're saying that it was only one site you were referring to and that his answer that he had read documents in relation to it confirmed the position for you. Thank you very much. That clears it up. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I would like to call up Exhibit Number 5D128.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, since the complete investigation was carried out by the military organs and once it was established that the army had not been involved in all that, the case continued to be processed by the district public prosecutor's office in Prizren. Please look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. The prosecutor is signed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In keeping with this document -- do you see the document before you? Do you agree with me that the investigation was taken over by the civilian prosecutor in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, please look at the document, see what it says in the document. Is this a document by which certain things are being handed over to the prosecutor in order to carry out certain procedures? Will you agree with me that the investigation was taken over by the civilian organs in keeping with the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who from. It does not come clear from this document that this was being taken over from somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Are they involved in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is very inappropriate, incorrect, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, what does the document in front of you mean? Can you please explain. Nothing else. That's all.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the title, this is an order for the exhumation by the district prosecutor's office. There's no word about any take-over.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now that we're on the subject of security organs, on Monday in response to the question put by Judge Bonomy you said that the commander of the security squad in the Pristina Corps was Nesic when you were there, in the Pristina Corps. Yesterday, in your evidence yesterday on page 81 you said that Nesic was in actual fact the security organ in the Pristina Military District. What is correct?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said any such thing. What is correct is that Nesic introduced himself to me invariably as the security organ after Vujisic was expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just a second. Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, corps command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify that first.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I never said anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But yesterday you said on page 81 in line 24 that Nesic was actually the security organ in the military district --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Have you heard the name of Momir Stojanovic, who at the time when Mr. Boris Tadic was minister of defence, was the chief of security of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The chief of the entire service of security, if I -- if I have the same person in mind. I know some other people by the name of Momir Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about this one, and do you know that this same gentleman was actually commander of the security of the Pristina Corps -- rather, the chief of the security organs of the Pristina Corps during the aggression against our country?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about this, Mr. Cepic. I hear it from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just clarify one more thing. Vukojica Vujisic was replaced from his duty because of poor performance; right?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told on account of good performance Cvijic, Nedeljko, with whom I started working in Kosovo together, told me that they expelled him because he was exceptionally professional and a high-quality officer --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We did not get the end of your answer there. Could you clarify it for us, please, Mr. Dorovic. You said that you were told that he was replaced on account of good performance and you said a little more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of lawful, honourable, and proper work. He filed criminal charges, criminal reports, because of serious crimes; that is the only reason why he was expelled. I know specifically and that was the explanation I was given and that's what Nesic told me, too, that he was expelled because of the criminal charges brought against Ristevski and Stefanovic. On that occasion when I explained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's fine. That's obviously much more than you said before. I just wanted to know what you had said before. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just need a minute to find something in the statement, please, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, I am going to quote paragraph 30 of your statement, the last sentence. "I then told Nesic that I would extend the investigation to include Vujisic and confront him with accusations to be involved in this crime. Nesic then cursed my mother," and so on and so forth. A few moments ago you said he was exceptionally proper, or rather, before that you said in your statement that you would extend the investigation so as to include Vujisic --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're forgetting something, Mr. Nesic [as interpreted], that Nesic expelled Vujisic. You're forgetting that I started working with new security organs led by Cvijic, Nedeljko.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But I'm asking you for a specific answer. How come there's such a big difference?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: There's no difference, is that your testimony, no difference in your different statements, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the interpretation to be recorded. I'm going to repeat. Two minutes ago you said that Vujisic was an exceptionally professional, conscientious, and responsible person.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what Nedeljko Cvijic told me the first evening when we met, and he explained it to me in great detail why it was that he had been expelled. He said that he had been expelled by the new people who came in and who now held all the strings in their hands and that they expelled him because he worked lawfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So why did you want to extend the investigation against Vujisic?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you are abusing this. Please read all of what I said. You will see that you are maliciously portraying this, taking it out of context. That is my answer to Nesic's assertion that Vujisic actually filed criminal report against the people he worked with, the security organs, because they did not share with him. That is what it says in my report, and I as prosecutor said in that case, Mr. Nesic [as interpreted], I would have to extend the investigation so as to include Vujisic if they shared this together, and then he said that he would expel me, that he didn't need somebody like that. He swore my mother -- he cursed my mother, he swore at me, and he left the office, so it would be fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just reading this. I read everything in detail and you say - your words are in the statement - "then I said to Nesic that I would extend the investigation so as to include Vujisic and to confront him with the accusations." Did you confront him with the accusations, did you extend the investigation, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was prevented by Nesic, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And why didn't you write an official note about this, that you were prevented in doing what you said previously?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And why are you prejudging this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Don't respond by putting questions to me. Let your answer be recorded in the transcript. Just take it easy, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So why did you not write an official note?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I did write an official note and that official note is one that the security organs are aware of. Colonel Kovac knows about this in the security administration; my commander, Pesic; and my superiors know about this. It was precisely at the very beginning that I indicated what Nesic's threats were and these were threats that were repeated throughout my stay down there. So there is an official note in which I portrayed what Nesic did to me, how he threatened me, how he stopped me from doing my work. There is a written record of this; that I be protected by the security organ of my command, because these are separate commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You wrote that the door on your car did not work properly, and that is what you wrote on the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that, Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm putting a question. Listen to me carefully.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, all right, I cannot tell the difference. Actually, I'm trying to understand your question. It seemed to me that you had put a question --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please do not interrupt me, please. I ask you kindly not to interrupt me. On the 30th of May you wrote - and we saw that in the courtroom yesterday - that the door on your car did not work properly and the language was pretty strong that you used in this letter to Colonel Pesic, the commander of the military district. Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's your question, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking about something different, very different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if you want to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yesterday while giving evidence, when Mr. Aleksic put a question to you, you said that on that day you submitted your request to be relieved of duty. Am I right if I say that it wasn't on the 30th of May that you submitted this request to be relieved of duty?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of June, that's when I submitted a formal request and I handed it in, but, Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we're on the subject of the 1st of June, yesterday you said that you were in detention until the 4th of June, 1999, in the evening. Could you tell me when you were actually detained.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Transcript page 97, line 5.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that practically I was in detention on the 4th of June, all day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry about that. Sorry. Sorry. It was only on the 4th of June that you were in detention?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. While Nesic was breaking up my office and taking documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And that day they probably took the documents for Ristevski?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he probably took them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Earlier --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the evening of the 29th. On that day he only broke into my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: On that -- [In English] "Tuesday on 29th" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that Mr. Cepic has to slow down with his questions and cannot overlap with the witness all the time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, it's a yellow card this time. The interpreter is again saying you must slow down. Now, what remedy do I have against you --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- am I going to have to ask someone else to conduct the cross-examination or are you going to do as requested?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise one more time, Your Honour. I especially apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will try to do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dorovic, up until the 4th of June, am I right if I say that you carried out your duties as prosecutor on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th in the morning, up until 10.00 in the morning, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And officially you were prosecutor all that time?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally, like usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also held meetings of your collegium, staff meetings with your colleagues from the prosecutor's office. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On four occasions on General Obrencevic's orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All the way up to the 4th?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, yesterday during the course of the day I received an e-mail, in my modest opinion, a very interesting document, and I asked for an urgent translation of that document. However, until this moment I do not have a translation of the document, so I ask very kindly -- actually, it's just arrived. It's just arrived, my colleague told me just now. So could we please call up on e-court 5D131.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I object to that. I haven't even seen the document. I mean, he may put a question on the basis of the document, but I object to the use of the document at this late point. He was obliged to give the documents he would use at the beginning of the cross-examination, which was yesterday in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the explanation's been given that he received it in the course of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours -- but, I don't know why he only received it yesterday. Did they only find it in their files late or what is the background? I don't think that can be a justification all the time just to say, I received it only yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I have to say I think the Defence have not abused the late -- the possibility of late introduction of documents in this case. I know it's happened occasionally, but my -- I don't have the impression that this is a regular piece of behaviour and deliberately done. I think there may be a couple of occasions where it's appeared that way, and we've dealt with them adequately. But it's unrealistic, I think, to say, Well, he can put questions based on the document but he can't submit the document, bearing in mind that actually proving it is something that probably has to await the presentation of the Defence case. So I don't think it's a particularly helpful way for the Prosecution to police the presentation of the Defence case to take exception to this. However, Mr. Cepic, I think if you could re-direct your cross-examination to something else for the moment and let Ms. Moeller have a copy of the document, then she'll be better prepared to deal with the issue when it arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please take these copies and for the sake of clarity, Your Honour, unfortunately, I only have four copies here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you move to something else and then come back to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, is it correct that before the municipal court in Nis under number K133/06 there were proceedings instituted against you because offence to an official person, that is to say, you offended Judge Zoran Popovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These proceedings were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We cannot deal with it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that what the e-mail is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour, and I just showed a copy of e-mail and the time when I received this copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think you should come back to it and give Ms. Moeller time to consider the position. So move on to something else just now and return to this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, is it correct that on a train between Belgrade and Bar, near the town of Prijepolje, you were preventing policemen from carrying out their duty when you took out your pistol when they asked you to show your ID, which is regular procedure. Could you tell us something about this?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, is it with regret that I have to say that this is a dirty lie, and that it is improper for you to bring something like that up in this honourable court. That is not true. This is a dirty lie that has been abused by the security organs. The case was quite different, and you are misrepresenting it maliciously in passing, which is really beneath the role that you're supposed to play here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D541 is the document that I would like the registrar to call up here, that is the last paragraph of that statement. Could we have the last page and the last paragraph of the document we see in e-court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, the penultimate paragraph. This is the testimony of one of the witnesses in the proceedings still pending against you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proceedings were not instituted against me, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. We'll see about that.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't take something that is untrue as your starting point. If you know the proceedings is not instituted against me but against the judges who --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dorovic. Why did you not bring along proof of the fact that the proceedings were not instituted against you?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have that. I do have proof of the fact that the judge, or rather, that the prosecutor dropped the charges and that the court issued two decisions. I asked the Chamber yesterday for permission to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you were referring to about the offence in Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not referring to that offence case. You would know very well what I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the decision about the termination of the proceedings that was issued by the district court in Belgrade. I spoke about that yesterday. What Djura Blagojevic states here is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly. Let us not jump from topic to topic. When was the decision terminating the proceedings against you issued at the military department of the district court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got it sometime in the middle of last year, in the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why don't we have it before us? You gave us a mountain of other documents.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why I should be giving anything to you, Mr. Cepic. If you ask me, then I'll give it to you. I'm offering it to you. Here. If you want to have it, I'll give it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why was the procedure before the district court in the military department launched?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For physical assault.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why was it terminated?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I received on the 26th of April a new indictment. A hearing was held thereupon, and subsequently the prosecutor dropped the charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When was this? When did the prosecutor drop the charges?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already that I was told in the month of July that the prosecutor had given up the charges. I have the decision concerning Nis and concerning that bodily harm which you showed -- which you presented as grievous bodily harm; whereas, it wasn't. And on the 26th of April, on the sixth hearing held in the case, I received an amended indictment. At the very next hearing there was a postponement. I asked for the trial to continue, and I was told that the prosecutor had given up the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But you did not ever receive a written document?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the proceedings are still pending against you?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Cepic. That's not true. There are no proceedings against me. There are, however, proceedings against them. There is another decision, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The 26th of April in which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2006, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you've heard -- after the postponement and when you were told that the prosecutor had given up the case, since then have you heard anything at all about these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that hearing, I asked for the proceeding to be brought to a close so that I'm not exposed to abuse any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please listen to my question. Since you were told that the prosecutor had given up the case, have you heard anything further about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't receive a document. I didn't hear anything else to that effect, but on that occasion I was told that the prosecutor had given up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Simple question, Mr. Dorovic. It appears, although you make it very difficult for us by not answering it directly, it appears that you have heard not one word about the matter since you were told in July that the proceedings had been dropped. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, in your system, would that normally suggest to you that that was the end of the matter, that now we are, what, nine months after July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, that would mean what you said. Two decisions were taken but a third one has to be taken still. I appealed to them to, in fact, issue such a decision because this has been going on for eight years now. 4

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So in your system a case can go on for nine months without anything actually happening in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it can. I wasn't summoned for two years, and now I'm speaking about my case. Of course matters should not proceed that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, can we go back to the exhibit that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I have the page before that in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Last page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, whoa. I'm asking to see some of this, Mr. Cepic You can go back to it in a moment. I'm just having a look at this page. Now, we heard yesterday, Mr. Cepic, about an allegation of a pistol being drawn, and I thought it was an in office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I will elucidate the matters in several of my questions. Yes, it did take place there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It was -- the allegation yesterday related to something in an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This allegation we're looking at here relates to something in a train. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Completely two different cases, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You wish to therefore contest the testimony of a sworn witness who testified against you?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat. It's a dirty lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll finish that. Let's just go back for one moment to the proceedings -- or rather, to the event on the 30th of May in the evening. We heard during the cross-examination by my learned friend Mr. Aleksic some details concerning this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the court deputy to call up Prosecution Exhibit P2708.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Dorovic, all of us who are married come into conflict more or less with our mothers-in-law. Did you ever come into conflict with your mother-in-law which ended up before a court?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, 25 years ago, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And this was processed before the Belgrade court, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not wish to speak about that, Mr. Cepic. This is a family matter that was dealt with and done with 25 years ago. This is something that only serves to speak about your person, Mr. Cepic. This was dealt with 25 years ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a purpose in this cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will change the topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the record -- oh, yes, we have it before us. This is the trial record.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the heading here it says that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, I've misunderstood you. I thought you were departing -- is there a reason for cross-examining the witness about a domestic event 25 years ago in a war crimes trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I just tried to check credibility of this witness how many times he was before the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are these --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How many times he was proceed before the courts of our country, how many times he was accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes and --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For which crimes he was accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And during what period of time are we talking?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That allegations were 20 years ago, but it was a criminal act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well -- just give us a moment until we consider this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will not allow you to ask any questions about the allegation that you've got on the screen at the moment and we will disregard it. Obviously, we have to deal with each allegation as it comes, but please depart from this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. I just tried to check his criminal record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but not all criminal records are relevant, Mr. Cepic, and we will ensure that we only consider ones that are relevant to issues before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you one more time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was never convicted and I'm 51 years old. Never ever was I convicted and I am 51 years old. Proceedings were terminated on several occasions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you accept that, that the witness has never been found guilty of any offence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this time I don't have a report from the criminal records in order to double-check this. The witness did say that he was being tried for this offence more than 20 years ago. We have a trial record in front of us which dates five years back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've already ruled on this one, Mr. Cepic. And unless you've got before you a foundation, something that tells you he was convicted of something, we will not allow you to ask any more questions about his past record.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't convicted ever. I am 51. It is true that three times there were -- on three occasions there were proceedings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're not interested in allegations of -- in the past history that were never -- that did not result in convictions because we are not here to investigate the rights and wrongs of events many years ago, other than -- by that, I mean many years before 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will I be allowed to put few questions concerning the proceedings instituted against Mr. Dorovic and this refers to the trial record that we see before us. This is tied with the period of time when he served as prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, these you can ask about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can this Exhibit P2708 be turned to page 7 in B/C/S and 10 in English. Could we also have the version in English, page 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, we have the trial record before us from the proceedings where you were accused --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I was accused, not am, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very well. We have the testimony by Witness Corac, who was a military police officer at the time and by profession a medical doctor, who testified he was unable to come closer to you because you trained your pistol at him whilst he was in the presence of two more police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 11 of the English translation. Paragraph 4 in English is where he states: "Back off, Corac. I will kill you all, motherfuckers." Let's carry on. Page 12 of the English translation and page 8 of the original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't want you to go through various paragraphs before posing a question. You should pose a question in relation to the paragraph you've just read. I think I indicated that at the outset today.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you in your evidence confirmed that you had trained your pistol on them and threatened them with killing them?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a falsified document, and because this trial record was falsified, the president of the district court is being held to account. A complete paragraph was left out and the president of the court and Judge Popovic are being tried for this very fact. Why are you concealing this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will get to that.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not a correct person, Mr. Cepic. This is a falsified document and there is a judge who is being held to account for the fact that the document is falsified. Are you aware of the fact that there is an investigation pending for this very fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dorovic, we received the document from the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As proof of fact that it's a falsification that the president of the court arranged for the falsification of the document and rigging a trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 5 of the original, and in English page 7, paragraph 2, the last sentence in English. And in the original it's the first paragraph, last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is your testimony at the trial where you confirm: "I did, indeed, say something along the lines of: 'Do not come closer. I will kill you. '"

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was after the physical conflict, after I had taken the police their pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You took a pistol off of a police officer?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a police officer's pistol and there is proof of fact whose pistol it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let me just go back to what you said. Thank you very much. Thank you very much, indeed. Let's go back to Mr. Corac's testimony, the testimony of Mr. Corac. Let's not elaborate on this too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8 of the original, please. Page 12 of the English version, paragraph 1 thereof. [In English] Your Honour, may I continue, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Corac introduced himself. He was a reserve military policeman. By profession he was a doctor. And he says in the last sentence that you didn't show any signs of fear at that time. Was he right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something for you to conclude when you analyse what he said, but you forget that before that, I had seized the pistol from them and that all this was happening in my office --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And at 22 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. I can't make any conclusions. I can't draw conclusions, but there are people who can and such conclusions were, indeed, drawn and in practice there are, as you may well know, drawn by professionals.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have Prosecution Exhibit P2706.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, in front of us on our screens we can see an opinion by Dr. Tomislav Krstovic, specialist in neuropsychiatry and forensic psychiatry. He says that a longer observation of the accused under hospital conditions is necessary, considering the complexity of the case. He had carefully looked at all the documents in the file and he inferred this conclusion and came up with this opinion. My question is very simple. To this very day, have you ever been checked in order to dispel doubts about your mental health?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was made null and void and this person is criminally charged for this order and you have just -- this was written in order to stop me talking at the moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Once the witness has said --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this was made null and void at the same moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... This is the sort of area that he should be free to deal with. We're not here to hear your speeches; we're here to hear his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Dorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank God that you have realised what this is all about. I'm not going to waste your time. I'll be very brief. In the district court in Belgrade proceedings are pending against the president of the military court, Vukadin Milojevic, and Judge Zoran Popovic for all they have done. They almost put me in an asylum in order to stop me from talking, to shut my mouth after the witnesses, the current judge, and current prosecutor of the district court had confirmed that I had been attacked, that I defended myself, and that I managed to defend both myself and them. The number of that case file is VP -- to be more precise, the district court in Belgrade military department, decision number is VP Ki 13 -- I apologise, 1738/2005. This is the trial to establish criminal responsibility for the fabrication of the record that you just a while ago allowed to be analysed before you. I am thankful to Mr. Cepic for having asked this question. I am only sorry that he did not put it earlier, but -- and I would like to thank you for giving me an opportunity to explain things. In this way Cepic wanted to discredit me as a witness. It's up to you to be the judge of everything, judging by everything that I said and everything I've been through, when the two witnesses said that I defended myself and that I defended them as well. And you should trust them because one of them is a judge and another is a prosecutor, very experienced people. All of this had been stopped, and proceedings are pending against all these people who fabricated all that. There's also a decision on dropping the charges, not of grave bodily harm but light bodily harm, and this is the essence of the matter. This document corroborates the fact that these proceedings were fabricated, that I was framed. And they told me that if I did not accept retirement, that if I did not forget everything that I had done, that I did not leave the army, that they would proclaim me insane. I sought protection from everybody I could in the country. I addressed everybody I possibly could address on that occasion. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dorovic. Could you deal with the particular question, as well: Have you ever been the subject of a psychiatric examination subsequent to this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never. There was no need for that. If you will allow me just one more explanation, Your Honours. In the army, if there are suspicions about the health of the officer, that officer has to undergo examinations, even against their will. So far I have not been put under that, and there have never been any suspicions about my mental health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you did not file charges against the doctor, but rather against Milojevic and Popovic?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And all those who were involved in the fabrication of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You did not raise charges against --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true there are criminal reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Slow down --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from the times when I wanted to challenge criminal responsibility of all these involved. I was summoned -- please don't do that. You cannot deal with this like that. If you want to discredit me, then this has to be done with a measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't do it this way, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How did you challenge the opinion of this doctor?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I filed a criminal report against him alleging that he participated --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Against the doctor --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against all who were involved in that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And about the doctor --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against the doctor as well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please, when I'm speaking -- when I'm speaking, I expect silence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you are the offender here, constantly overrunning the witness, who's answering questions which he's entitled to answer in the way he's choosing to do because of the challenge you are making against him. So please allow him to answer these questions. When I think he's gone too far, I'll stop him. Now, let's start this exercise again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can you please bear with me just for a moment while I look for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to ask Mr. Registrar to tender Exhibit Number 2724, please, P2724.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dorovic, this is a criminal report for the crime of violation of law on the part of the judges that you filed against Vukadin Milojevic, president of the court in Nis; Radenko Miladinovic, judge of the military court in Nis; and an unidentified general from the military leadership.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I said that it was Radomir Gojovic, and you know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This was a plot against you wasn't it, conspiracy?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may call it whatever. I filed a report on them making efforts to put me to trial, and you can call it whatever. You can call it a conspiracy. Maybe this is part of your effort to discredit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The judge in your proceedings was Zoran Popovic, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, no, let me be very precise. It was Radenko Miladinovic who learned about that, and he wanted to be removed from the case, because it was well known that he had been tried in a number of fabricated cases. And he wanted to be excluded from these proceedings, and that is why he was indeed excluded; and then this was given to Popovic and he continued in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the meantime, you were prosecuted by the prosecutor for offending Popovic?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about later. These proceedings were stayed because of the amendments to the criminal law, and Mr. Popovic did not want to join the prosecution against you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is prosecuted ex officio, and the prosecutor abandoned the charges. He dropped the case 93 pursuant to Article 101. Mr. Cepic, at the time when this insult allegedly took place, this was prosecuted ex officio. And he dropped the charges because there was no insult, and it had -- it was proven that the proceedings had been fabricated and that's why he is now criminal charged not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have Prosecution Exhibit P2770.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In front of us we have a decision dropping the proceedings against you for another crime, crime of insult, and in the statement of reasons it says: "The criminal proceedings against the accused Lakic Dorovic, lieutenant-colonel, serving with the Ministry of Defence for crime of insult from Article 1993 [as interpreted], paragraph 2 has abandoned the pursuit of prosecution for this criminal act"?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that pursuant to Article 101, the acts are prosecuted ex officio. You may be right that this may be wrong, because this is prosecuted ex officio and you know it only too well. This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me go back to the previously mentioned criminal report?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now call up exhibit number P2694.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the higher instance, the higher judiciary instance, issued this decision on the screen to turn down your application?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why are you talking about a document which has been ruled out for a long time?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So this has been ruled out?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have a decision on new proceedings. Why are you talking about a decision which is no longer topical? This is just one in a series of your incorrect actions. You are a good lawyer, but this is obviously malicious on your part. Why are you not showing us the decision that is in place, that is effective now, because there are proceedings underway now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's look at the last paragraph of this document. In your appeal, you expanded on the allegation. You have mentioned some war crimes but not a specific one, and the supreme military court finds that if you had learned about crimes as an official person pursuant to Articles 2 and 3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 223 .

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- of the ZKP, the law on criminal proceedings, you are duty-bound to report such acts to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true, Mr. Cepic, and I reported on those in 1999 to everybody in the state, including the state federal prosecutor. Mr. Cepic, you have just shown us a criminal report. The Court has to bear in mind that I addressed the supreme military prosecutor, not Milosavljevic at the first-instance court who was ordained with the three ranks in a scope of 14 months and you have to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You cannot be promoted in service because there are all -- still proceedings against you pending, and you cannot be promoted to the rank of colonel because of the proceedings that are pending against you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, let my superiors talk about that, but the fact is I was the first one put forth for promotion and that the decision was prepared with the signature of the president of the republic on my republic. But because of the conflict with the security organ, it was from -- by them that I was put forth in 2002 for the position of the military prosecutor in Belgrade. You have to know that. There is written document to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But in keeping with the letter of the law, you cannot be promoted in the military service because --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be appointed as a prosecutor, I cannot be appointed as a judge, and I have to suffer abuse. I have to continue suffering abuse. You're very right, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Because there are proceedings pending against you?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were proceedings against me. There were, and I am repeating it for the third time, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why they don't intend to finish the proceedings. They are waiting for me to either be retired or to die. However, I'm still alive, and I still haven't fled the way they've fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, will you allow me to go back to an exhibit that I received yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or rather, the exhibit that I received yesterday, and in that way I will finish my cross-examination? Thank you. Could we see in e-court Defence Exhibit 5D131.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dorovic, you confirmed to us that on the 1st of June, you were in your office, the prosecutor's office, that you had meetings, that you were informed about everything. Please take a careful look at this document in front of you. You said previously that Ristevski, Zoran, and Stefanovic, Aleksandar, are the cases that were stolen before that on the 29th of May. We have here a judgement of the military court attached to the command of the military district of Pristina on the day of June 1st, 1999, dealing with Ristevski and Stefanovic.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, with full responsibility before this Court and before all courts in this world, with full responsibility before God I, claim that Ristevski was not tried at the time when I was in Kosovo; that is to say, until the 4th of June, 1999, at 10.00 in the morning, I claim to you, with full responsibility, that Ristevski was not tried and that this trial was not attended by prosecution attorneys. I would have been present had there been a trial. This is a forgery. I'm aware of the gravity of what I'm saying; but up until the 4th of June, Ristevski was not tried. Most probably this is a forgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dorovic.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're more than welcome, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just have a mistake in translation. In introduction part, there is -- this is marked 1st of May, 1999; but in original document, it is 1st of June, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The document says the hearing was on the 1st of May. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It is mistake. If you see the previous part of sentence, first military prosecutor criminal number 390/99, dated 22nd May 1999, after a public hearing held on 1st May. In original document, it is the 1st of June. Even the witness confirmed that the indictment is issued on 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the indictment was, but there is this other indictment, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cepic, please don't deal with it so partially. Let us get to the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've heard that there's another indictment earlier in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And also, by your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The crime is formulated in a different way here. Everything is different here. You cannot see who prosecution counsel is. And since these charges are brought ex officio, you cannot do that without the actual prosecuting attorney involved. It's not a proposal to take to court to prosecute --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Wait a second. You said it was not a proposal to prosecute?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about two indictments, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Here it says in the introductory part: "Deciding in accordance with the proposal to prosecute of the military prosecutor" --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, everybody can read what is written here. The Court can read it for themselves, too, but I am telling you that these are proceedings regarding two indictments; then you know full well what indictments are, what proposals to indict or prosecute are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. And you said yesterday that these indictments are registered as 3D0/99 [as interpreted]; right, of the 22nd --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, two; both are the 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 3D0/99 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3D0/91 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you didn't mention 91 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please slow down. It's got to the stage where I will have to take action because you've been asked repeatedly both of you --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- to take this much more slowly and observe a pause. This is not appropriate behaviour in a courtroom. So please --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, Your Honour, I promise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you allow me, we have a problem in transcript page 42, line 14 and 15, it is not 3D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's also in line 12, it's 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, I said 390/99.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there you're finding the sort of problem that arises when you speak too quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise one more time. Thank you, Your Honours, that was my last and final question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dorovic, thank you for the answers you gave. Please don't take this personally because this is the way things go in a cross-examination, and we are professionals here. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even that does not mean behaving in an inappropriate way. You are a very professional man, and you know that you acted very unfairly today. I had a different impression of what your role was supposed to be and a different role of what you personally were supposed to be like. I am disappointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm glad I met you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, there is, Your Honour. Could we maybe -- would you like me to start right now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: -- or take a break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. The break today should have been five minutes ago. And we will take the break now and we will resume at 11.00. Mr. Dorovic, we need to have a break at this time. It's a bit earlier than yesterday, but that's for our own technical reasons. Would you again go with the usher from the courtroom and we'll see you again at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sir, I just have a couple of questions to clarify some points from the cross-examination of the counsel for you. And let's start with the issues we discussed just this morning. The proceedings regarding this brawl you had with your deputy while you were in Pristina still. On that day that this event occurred, what had happened in the morning?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 30th of May in the morning, for the umpteenth time, Nesic walked in and he presented me with an ultimatum, asking me to drop criminal charges and he threatened me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And if I --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: -- if I can interrupt you here. I was just trying to clarify. Is that the day -- was that the same day that this brawl occurred in the evening where in the morning Nesic threatened you in regard to these files, Ristevski and Stefanovic? That was all on one day, was it?

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was the fourth time. I have this precisely recorded in my diary, and I can refer to the dates --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you --

utterances.speaker: LAKIC DOROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the first time was on the 26th and this was on the 30th -- well, yes. I would like to emphasise that these were --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just trying to clarify the chronology of the events here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
